headline: Expect warm, dry weather through Thanksgiving and Black Friday, with coastal valleys like Glendale reaching the mid 70s to lower 80s by Friday, while the big concern is the coast: a Coastal Flood Watch Wednesday–Thursday for very high morning tides plus a large west swell.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A few leftover showers may linger off the Los Angeles County coast and near Catalina Island early Monday, but otherwise Monday and Monday night are mild and dry, including around Glendale and Burbank. A Frost Advisory runs until 8 AM Monday for the Antelope Valley and its eastern foothills, with lows of 33 to 35 and locally 32; other inland areas come close but clouds should keep them a bit warmer. Low clouds and fog form overnight in interior San Luis Obispo County, including the Salinas Valley, and burn off by late morning.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Weak high pressure and light offshore (northeast) winds bring warm, dry weather Tuesday, with highs in the 60s and 70s across the coasts and coastal valleys, including the Glendale area. A weakening cold front brushes the Central Coast Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, but it now looks drier, with generally a tenth of an inch of rain or less there; Los Angeles and Ventura counties have less than a 10 percent chance of measurable rain. Most areas actually warm a bit Wednesday as high pressure builds in behind the front.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday look warm and dry under strong high pressure with weak to moderate offshore winds. Highs peak Friday in the mid 70s to lower 80s along the coast and in the coastal valleys, about 10 degrees cooler inland, averaging 8 to 12 degrees above normal. Northeast winds should stay below advisory levels, though gusts of 40 to 45 mph are possible Thursday morning in the western San Gabriel and Santa Susana mountains (a very low chance of a Wind Advisory). There is a strong signal for a return to a stormier pattern around the end of the month into early December, possibly a series of storms, but details are fuzzy.

coast: Forecasters have significant concern for moderate to major coastal flooding Thanksgiving week from a combination of unusually high sea levels (warm ocean water expanding), extra-high tides with the moon at its closest, and a large long-period west swell. For the Central Coast, Ventura and Los Angeles counties, a Coastal Flood Advisory runs until 3 AM Wednesday (shallow flooding of beach parking lots and unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion), followed by a Coastal Flood Watch from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon, when peak high tides between 8:45 and 10 AM reach about 8.2–8.4 feet for LA/Ventura and 7.9–8.2 feet for the Central Coast, with a reasonable worst case 0.3–0.5 foot higher; if upgraded to a warning, expect more extensive flooding farther inland, likely damage to coastal roads and structures, and significant beach erosion. Areas of greatest concern are Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and Long Beach/Naples in LA County, Faria to Silver Strand Beach and Ventura Harbor in Ventura County, and Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes and the Cayucos, Avila and Pismo piers on the Central Coast; the Santa Barbara South Coast (Santa Barbara to Rincon, Jalama Beach) and the Catalina and Santa Barbara islands have a Coastal Flood Advisory through Thursday, with more hazards likely Friday. A High Surf Advisory covers the Central Coast until 3 PM Thursday: surf up to 11 feet Monday morning, a lull Monday night into Tuesday, then rapid building to 10–15 feet Wednesday morning and 15–22 feet Wednesday afternoon and evening, likely upgraded to a High Surf Warning by Tuesday, with breaking waves at the Morro Bay entrance Wednesday and possibly Thursday. LA and Ventura beaches see elevated to high surf all week, peaking Wednesday and Thursday with likely High Surf Advisories, a small chance of warning-level surf up to 15 feet on the Ventura coast, and breaking waves at the Ventura Harbor entrance Wednesday; stay off rock jetties and away from the water's edge. Offshore, winds and seas stay below small craft advisory levels through Tuesday night, then low-end advisory-level northwest to west winds are possible Wednesday and Wednesday night south of Point Conception as a 14–16 foot west swell brings large seas to the outer waters.
watch_for: Coastal Flood Watch late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon: morning high tides plus a big west swell could bring moderate to major flooding at LA, Ventura and Central Coast beaches and harbors.
Gusts of 40 to 45 mph possible Thursday morning in the western San Gabriel and Santa Susana mountains.
A possible return to stormier weather around the end of November into early December.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the warm, dry stretch through Black Friday and that the midweek front stays weak, and say the end-of-month stormy pattern is likely but its details are still unclear.
